If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is rising, cap forecast growth at 1.0% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent momentum overextension.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is volatile, add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for sentiment-driven spikes.  
When sentiment drops sharply (from 0.67 to 0.00 within 3 days), reduce forecast by 2.0–3.0% for the next 5 days to reflect risk reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) across 5+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon to capture sentiment-driven tailwinds.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3% in early horizon and sentiment is positive, adjust downward by 1.0–2.0% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
